airport_class: business-aviation airport
mro_on_field: full bizjet handling; Dassault home market
how_unusual_foreign_state_jet: NOT UNUSUAL. The busiest business-aviation airport in Europe; no scheduled commercial passenger service since 1980. TRANSIT / STAGING ONLY - 18 logged legs, the single most-used field in the record, and no Kirk or TPUSA claim at any of them.
innocent_explanation: The mandatory mid-point of the Cairo-to-North-America route: Cairo->Le Bourget runs 3:56 to 4:22 on every logged leg; Le Bourget->US entry field runs 8:03 to 9:58.

airport_class: public-use commercial / general aviation
is_us_customs_port: yes - well-established East Coast customs and fuel stop
military_colocation: Delaware Air National Guard on field
how_unusual_foreign_state_jet: NOT unusual. KILG is a standard transatlantic corporate customs-and-fuel stop in the Philadelphia-Baltimore-Washington corridor without the slot pressure of the major hubs. It appears on 15 of the logged legs because it is the outbound customs stop, not because of Delaware.
innocent_explanation: Outbound US customs and fuel before the Atlantic crossing. NOT TO BE CONFUSED WITH Wilmington, North Carolina (ILM) - a live source-confusion risk on this page.

airport_class: public-use regional / municipal
is_us_customs_port: no - not a routine international port of entry
military_colocation: none on field; Camp Williams / Dugway Proving Ground elsewhere in Utah
mro_on_field: Duncan Aviation (full-service airframe, engine, avionics, paint, interior)
how_unusual_foreign_state_jet: GENUINELY UNUSUAL. Runway length is not the issue - it takes a Falcon 7X or a G-IV easily. What Provo lacks is the customs, protocol and handling infrastructure a foreign state aircraft normally needs. Every one of these aircraft entered the US somewhere else and reached Provo on a DOMESTIC leg.
innocent_explanation: Duncan Aviation runs an MRO on the field and has held the Egyptian Air Force maintenance account since 1999 (John Cullen). Two Provo-Provo closed-loop sorties (SU-BGM 10 Apr 2025, 55 min; SU-BND 5 Sep 2025, 68 min) are the classic post-maintenance functional check-flight signature.

airport_class: commercial service / joint civil-military
is_us_customs_port: limited - customs facilities are limited; Omaha handles the entry
military_colocation: Nebraska Air National Guard on field
mro_on_field: Duncan Aviation HEADQUARTERS and main plant - one of the largest privately-owned business-aviation MRO facilities in the world
how_unusual_foreign_state_jet: LESS unusual than it looks once Duncan is on the map. A Lincoln arrival by a foreign-registered bizjet is what a Duncan maintenance visit looks like. What IS notable is the repetition and the Omaha-then-Lincoln two-hop.
innocent_explanation: Duncan Aviation HQ. The Omaha->Lincoln 15-20 minute repositioning hop is the customs-then-shop signature, not a second destination. Anyone counting airport visits off a leg list double-counts one arrival.

airport_class: commercial service international - largest airport in Nebraska
is_us_customs_port: yes - US Customs and Border Protection facilities
military_colocation: Offutt AFB is a separate field ~10 mi south (USSTRATCOM)
how_unusual_foreign_state_jet: NOT unusual on its own. Eppley is a customs port of entry; it is exactly where an inbound foreign aircraft should clear.
innocent_explanation: Customs. The aircraft clears at Omaha and repositions to Lincoln for Duncan. This is the operational reason for the split.

airport_class: joint civil / military; Canadian airport of entry (CBSA)
military_colocation: 5 Wing Goose Bay, Royal Canadian Air Force; Cold War USAF Strategic Air Command host; NATO low-level training
how_unusual_foreign_state_jet: NOT UNUSUAL. It is THE classic North Atlantic technical stop - built 1941 for the ferry route, sitting on the great-circle line at roughly the point a range-limited aircraft runs out of fuel. TRANSIT ONLY; no Kirk or TPUSA claim here.
innocent_explanation: Fuel. Every logged stop is roughly one hour on the ground.

airport_name: Wichita Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport
airport_class: commercial service international
military_colocation: McConnell AFB is a separate field ~7 mi southeast
mro_on_field: Yingling Aviation - FAA Part 145 repair station servicing Dassault Falcon aircraft; Dassault-Wichita State ties since 2015
how_unusual_foreign_state_jet: NOT unusual for a Falcon. Wichita is the American general-aviation manufacturing capital and holds a Falcon-authorised service centre.
innocent_explanation: Yingling Aviation Falcon service. Three of the four logged Wichita stays are by Falcon 7X airframes.

airport_class: small commercial service international
military_colocation: Minot AFB ~13 mi north: 5th Bomb Wing (B-52H) and 91st Missile Wing (Minuteman III) - one of few installations hosting TWO legs of the US nuclear triad
how_unusual_foreign_state_jet: UNUSUAL AS A CHOICE, ordinary as a mechanism. Minot carries the International designation, so it is a legal first point of landing from abroad; but it is a very small field to pick for that. Its proximity to Minot AFB is the fact posters seize on. TRANSIT STOP ONLY - nobody claims a Kirk or TPUSA presence here.
innocent_explanation: It is the shortest legal customs entry on the great-circle line from Europe to Utah. Four of the five aircraft entered the US via Minot en route to Provo.
